description: A musical nasal sound emitted from the nasal passage (Al-Khayshoom). Occurs on Noon Mushaddadah (نّ) and Meem Mushaddadah (مّ), held for 2 counts (Harakatan).
practiceTips: Ensure the air flows strictly through the nose without tightening the vocal cords.

description: Merging of a vowelless letter (Noon Sakinah or Tanween) into the following letter from 'ي-ر-م-ل-و-ن'. Divided into Idgham with Ghunnah (ي-ن-م-و) and Idgham without Ghunnah (ر-ل).
practiceTips: Merge seamlessly into the second letter without pronouncing an independent Noon.

description: Pronouncing Noon Sakinah or Tanween in an intermediate state between Izhar (clarity) and Idgham (merging), retaining a 2-count nasal Ghunnah before the 15 Ikhfa letters (ت ث ج د ذ ز س ش ص ض ط ظ ف ق ك).
practiceTips: Place your tongue near the articulation point of the next letter while vibrating the nasal cavity.

description: Converting Noon Sakinah or Tanween into a concealed Meem with Ghunnah when followed by the letter Baa (ب). Indicated in the script by a miniature Meem (مـۭ).
practiceTips: Bring the lips together gently without pressing hard, sounding a soft Meem with nasal resonance.

description: Pronouncing Noon Sakinah or Tanween clearly from its origin without extra prolongation or nasalization before the 6 throat letters (ء هـ ع ح غ خ).
practiceTips: Pronounce the Noon clearly and decisively without lingering.

description: A bouncing or reverberating echo sound produced when pronouncing one of the letters of 'قُطْبُ جَدٍ' (ق ط ب ج د) when Sakin (bearing a Sukoon or when stopping on it).
practiceTips: Release the articulation point with a sharp, crisp bounce without turning it into a Fathah or Kasrah.

description: Prolongation of the voice through the Madd letters (Alif preceded by Fatha, Waw preceded by Damma, Ya preceded by Kasra). Range: Asli/Tabi'ee (2 counts) to Fara'ee (Mutasil, Munfasil, Lazim: 4, 5, or 6 counts).
practiceTips: Keep timing consistent: measure counts evenly like clapping or tapping your fingers rhythmically.
